payment-service request_rate stayed flat at ~100 req/s (mean 100.52) with no retry storm or traffic surge; affected payments are being parked in state 'PENDING_RETRY' rather than surfacing as synchronous HTTP 5xx, which is consistent with the aggregate error_rate staying green.

tasks.objective: Establish the true symptom onset time and blast radius. Look beyond the aggregate payment-service error_rate: query logs/metrics for payment-service and its neighbors around 12:15-13:59Z for transfer failure signatures (timeouts, connection resets, HTTP 4xx/5xx, retry storms, queue depth/backlog, latency p99, thread pool saturation, DB or broker errors). Determine which endpoints/operations fail, whether failures are customer-facing only via a specific path, and whether the green error-rate panel is a real signal or a coverage gap.
tasks.answer: The true symptom onset is 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (first error log 12:15:27Z), triggered by the expiry of the payment-service mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) used against bank-partner-api. The blast radius is essentially all outbound bank transfers to the bank partner: bank_api_error_rate=100% and payment_success_rate collapsed to ~2.5% for the entire 12:15-13:59Z window. The green error-rate panel is a real coverage gap, not a real signal — the aggregate error_rate (HTTP 5xx) stayed at ~0.21% and latency flat, because failed transfers are parked as PENDING_RETRY rather than returned as 5xx. This is not a client-app or bank-side issue.

tasks.objective: Find what changed and when across ALL services (not just payment-service): list deployments, config/feature-flag changes, and their timestamps for payment-service, its direct dependencies (bank/gateway connector, auth, DB, broker), and shared components in the 12:00-13:59Z window. Also map payment-service's dependency graph and check historical incidents for this signature.
tasks.answer: Across ALL services there were ZERO deployments in the 12:00-13:59Z incident window; the only nearby deployment is settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30Z (live, not rolled back). Exactly one config change exists: payment-service 'bank.api.timeout_ms' 3000->5000 at 11:20Z by p.nair ('Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'), ~1h before the ~12:17Z onset. payment-service depends on ledger-db (shared: also order/portfolio/settlement), kafka (shared) and bank-partner-api (external, no telemetry), behind api-gateway. The closest historical precedent is HIST-105 (bank partner API 5xx causing payment failures) and HIST-114 (ledger-db WAL disk-full write failures) - leads only, not evidence.

tasks.objective: Correlate the changes and dependency graph from task b against the actual onset time and failing path identified in task a: identify which change (if any) coincides with onset, whether the failure point sits in payment-service or a shared/downstream component, and return prior incident precedents that match this pattern.
tasks.answer: No change coincides with the onset: there were zero deployments across all services in 12:10-12:20Z (and none 11:00-13:59Z), and the only nearby change is payment-service 'bank.api.timeout_ms' 3000->5000 at 11:20Z, ~55 min earlier - it cannot explain a failure that started at 12:15Z. The failing path is the external edge payment-service -> bank-partner-api (has_telemetry=false), reached via api-gateway, and NOT the shared ledger-db/kafka components (ledger-db is shared by order/portfolio/settlement too, but only the payment bank edge failed). Precedents matching this pattern: HIST-106 (2025-06-30, settlement-service mTLS client certificate expired, no renewal automation, category credential_expiry) is the closest - same failure mode; HIST-105 (2025-11-19, bank partner API 5xx payment outages) matches the symptom but a different mechanism.

From the 'expired certificate (alert 45)' entries and message payloads, determine whether the chain LEAF is CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal (our client cert, caller side => H1) or a bank-partner-api server/intermediate cert (partner side => H2). tasks.answer: The chain LEAF is OUR client cert, not a bank cert: all 7 untruncated 'expired certificate (alert 45)' entries name 'our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z', and all 7 paired mTLS-handshake failures are 'mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected'. This supports H1 (caller-side client cert expiry) and gives no support to H2 (no partner server/intermediate cert is named). No bank-partner-api call logged an INFO-level SUCCESS in the 5 minutes before 12:15:00Z (0 matches, untruncated) — though payment-service never logs bank success at INFO at all, so that absence is expected and not itself evidence of a failed pre-onset call.

tasks.answer: No certificate/secret inventory record was retrievable via the tools available to me: the config-change surface for payment-service (and all services) over 2026-03-25..2026-04-02 shows exactly ONE change — key 'bank.api.timeout_ms' 3000->5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z — with no certificate/secret entry, and no cert-inventory tool exists in my toolset. I therefore CANNOT confirm the inventory-recorded notAfter for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal nor whether renewal automation is mapped to it (only precedent found is HIST-106: 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation', settlement-service). Separately, no certificate/secret rotation event or vendor advisory affecting bank-partner-api's trust anchor or leaf was found for 2026-03-25..2026-04-02: get_config_changes for bank-partner-api returned an empty list (count=0) and for all services returned only the timeout change. This neither confirms nor excludes a partner-side rotation — H2 stays unsupported by absence of evidence (bank-partner-api has no telemetry). The 12:15:00Z expiry attribution to OUR cert rests on payment-service runtime logs (team F7/F11), not on any inventory or advisory source.

critiques.summary: H1 (payment-service mTLS client cert expired at 12:15Z breaking the bank-partner-api edge) is strongly grounded and well-time-bounded: onset = notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, first ERROR 12:15:27Z, bank_api_error_rate=100% on 105/105 buckets, payment_success_rate ~2.5%, no deploy anywhere in window, and a same-class precedent (HIST-106: settlement-service client cert expired, no renewal automation). The "parked in PENDING_RETRY so aggregate error_rate stays green" mechanism is evidenced by flat request_rate/latency and green error_rate. H2 is not fully refuted: it is currently rejected only on the strength of the caller-side interpretation of the 'alert 45 / expired certificate; our client cert CN=...' text. The ambiguous phrase 'our client cert' is a label that could also be an operator-side description of the certificate the client presented/validated, and the only objective discriminator (does the chain show our leaf as expired) has not been read. Because H1 vs H2 name different origins and different fixes (renew/replace our client cert vs escalate to vendor), I am not accepting yet. H3/H4 rejections are sound (no timeout error class, latency flat, failure localized to the bank edge while other shared-db consumers are silent). Confidence capped at 0.75 pending the discriminator.

challenges.issue: The single load-bearing claim (the expired cert is OUR client cert, caller-side) rests on error text that says 'our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=...', but the actual certificate chain (leaf vs intermediate) that produced 'alert 45' was never read. The chain direction is the only objective discriminator vs H2, and it is currently taken from a human-readable label inside an error string.

F7 log result is explicitly TRUNCATED (312 matched entries, 311 ERROR + 1 WARN) and an earlier INFO-level query (to 12:20Z) failed with 503, so the pre-onset baseline (did bank calls succeed before 12:15? any earlier cert/retry warnings?) is unverified. Onset is bounded below only by the error text itself, which is circular for the H1-vs-H2 question.

Dismissed largely on assumption: 'a partner-side TLS change could not produce text naming our own cert / alert 45.' That is plausible but untested. Partner telemetry is permanently unavailable (has_telemetry=false), so a vendor-side rotation cannot be excluded from change history alone; the discriminating evidence must come from the certificate chain, not from partner data.

Blast-radius/scope checks for the other shared ledger-db consumers (order-, portfolio-, settlement-service) in 12:15-13:59Z were never run, so H4 is excluded by argument (error signature is TLS) rather than by observed silence of the co-dependents. This is corroborating, not blocking.

Confidence 0.82 is above what the *ambiguous* discriminator supports; the ranking is nonetheless correct in the sense that H1 remains the only hypothesis positively evidenced (H2 has no positive evidence, only absence of refutation).

critiques.summary: H1 (payment-service mTLS client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 12:15:00Z, breaking the bank-partner-api edge) remains the best-supported hypothesis and is now better grounded than in round 1: onset is tightly bounded by notAfter=12:15:00Z against first ERROR 12:15:27Z (F7/F11), the failure is on the external bank edge only (F15/F16), bank_api_error_rate=100% on 105/105 buckets with payment_success_rate ~2.5% (F9), zero deployments and only one unrelated config change 55 min earlier (F1/F2/F13/F14), and a same-class precedent HIST-106 (client cert expired, no renewal automation) (F17/F21). My round-1 discriminator request was answered as fully as the toolset permits: the untruncated alert-45 chain names OUR client cert as the expired leaf and no bank server/intermediate CN (F23/F24/F27), and no partner rotation/advisory exists in inventory (F20/F22). H3/H4 rejections are sound and H2 is now contradicted by the only observable evidence, so the remaining distance is confirmation, not discrimination. I therefore do not treat the residual H2 ambiguity (partner has has_telemetry=false; notAfter confirmed only from runtime logs, not inventory) as grounds to keep querying — it is an assumption plus a confidence cap. Cap raised 0.75 -> 0.82: two independent signals (100% bank_api_error_rate for 105/105 buckets spanning the whole window, and 100%-correlated customer tickets) plus a fully-read error chain naming our own cert is strong, but the expiry instant still rests on one log surface and the partner's state is unobservable, so I will not defend 0.9. The generated 'open questions' (panel exclusion rule, last-good bank call, other ledger-db consumers) are worth a low-cost opportunistic check but are not blocking and should not delay mitigation.

challenges.issue: The 12:15:00Z expiry instant is asserted only from payment-service runtime error text (F7/F11); no cert/secret inventory record or renewal-automation mapping was retrievable (T5, F19/F22), so the HIST-106 'no renewal automation' parallel is by analogy, not confirmed. Holds for the origin but leaves the artifact capping cert unverified.

'~100% of transfers cannot be submitted to the bank' rests on bank_api_error_rate=100% and payment_success_rate~2.5% (F9), but the PENDING_RETRY-parking mechanism that keeps aggregate error_rate green is inferred from flat request_rate/latency (F10) rather than from a verified retry/state-machine counter. Secondary to the origin; affects the crispness of the impact statement.

Not positively refuted by partner-side telemetry (bank-partner-api has_telemetry=false); rejected on the caller-side wording of the alert-45 payloads and absence of any rotation/advisory record (F20/F22/F23/F27). The absence is consistent with H1 but not independently corroborating. This is the main reason confidence is capped at 0.82 rather than higher.

Ruled out by argument (failure localized to payment-service's bank edge; other ledger-db consumers not implicated, F15/F16) rather than by reading order-/portfolio-/settlement-service telemetry for 12:15-13:59Z. Low risk given the TLS error class is absent for those services' shared path.
